title: Sell Mineral Rights in Pyote, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Pyote, TX | Ward County Buyer
metaDescription: Pyote, TX minerals sit in Ward County oil country going back generations. Get an honest valuation from someone who reads the well records, not a mailer.
heroLead: Pyote is a small Ward County town best known locally for the old Rattlesnake Bomber Base from World War II, but the ground around it has a longer history in oil than in aviation.
intro: There's not much left standing at the old airbase east of town, but the oilfield history in this part of Ward County runs deeper and longer. Pyote sits among decades of legacy vertical production, with newer horizontal development from the busier Delaware Basin counties to the south reaching this direction in recent years.

sections.heading: A small town with old oil paper
paragraphs: Because Pyote never grew large, a lot of the surrounding mineral ownership has stayed within the same small number of original ranching and homestead families for generations, split among heirs who may now live well outside West Texas. Leases here are often decades old and held by production on modest, steady vertical wells.

sections.heading: Checking whether newer drilling has reached your acreage
paragraphs: Horizontal Wolfcamp development pushing north from Reeves and Loving counties has been extending into parts of Ward County, including acreage near Pyote. If your family's interest has sat quiet for years, it's worth a quick check on current permits before assuming nothing's changed.

sections.heading: What decades-old vertical leases mean for a sale today
paragraphs: A lot of the leases covering acreage near Pyote were signed when a single well might be considered a good day's work, long before anyone was running horizontal laterals through this rock. Those leases are typically still valid as long as production hasn't lapsed, and the royalty terms in them often predate the higher royalty fractions operators negotiate today.

That doesn't mean the interest is stuck at 1950s value. If a new operator wants to redrill the acreage horizontally, they generally have to negotiate a new lease once the old one expires or renegotiate terms, and that can meaningfully change what your interest is worth going forward, even if the current check is modest.

faqs.question: Is there still active oil production around Pyote?
faqs.answer: Yes, mostly legacy vertical wells with newer horizontal development from the south extending into some acreage. We check current permits near your specific tract to see which applies to you.

faqs.question: My family's lease near Pyote is from decades ago and I've lost track of the paperwork. What now?
faqs.answer: Send whatever you have, even a check stub or an old lease. We use Ward County clerk records in Monahans to confirm current ownership and any missing details.

faqs.question: Does the old bomber base affect mineral rights nearby?
faqs.answer: No, it's a separate historical site with no bearing on mineral ownership or production in the surrounding area.

faqs.question: Is my old Pyote-area lease still valid if the well has been producing continuously?
faqs.answer: Generally, yes. Most leases here are held by production, meaning they remain valid as long as the well continues producing, regardless of how old the original lease document is.
